extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and standards governing specified reply time limits, shortened statutory periods, extensions of time (37 CFR 1.136), consequences of late or omitted replies, holidays/weekend rules, and when reply periods are restarted or reset during patent prosecution before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to timely reply to petition for access
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Office gives an applicant a specified time (usually 3 weeks) to state objections to granting a petition for access, the failure to timely reply will not affect prosecution (assuming the application is still pending), but will result in the Office rendering a decision on the petition for access without considering any objections by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete IDS — time to complete and consequence of failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an information disclosure statement complies with 37 CFR 1.97 but part of the content requirement of 37 CFR 1.98 has been inadvertently omitted, the examiner may set a 1-month time limit for completion of the information disclosure statement; failure to timely comply will not result in abandonment but the IDS will be placed in the file with the noncomplying information not being considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 609.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse of restriction requirement — time to cancel nonelected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is otherwise allowable but contains a traverse of a restriction requirement, the applicant may be given a specified time (e.g., a 1-month time limit) to cancel claims to the nonelected invention or species or take other appropriate action (e.g., petition the restriction requirement under 37 CFR 1.144); failure to timely file a petition under 1.144 (or cancel the claims) will not result in abandonment but will be treated as authorization to cancel the claims to the nonelected invention or species and the application will be passed to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.141 and 1.144, and MPEP §§821.01 and 821.04(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested claims to provoke interference — effect of noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may require an applicant to add a claim to provoke an interference; failure to satisfy the requirement within a period (not less than one month) the examiner sets will operate as a concession of priority for the subject matter of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The failure to timely present the suggested claim will not result in abandonment but will be treated as a concession by the applicant of the priority of the subject matter of the claim. See MPEP Chapter 2300 and 37 CFR 41.202(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set time when failure may lead to abandonment — specify extension exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the failure to take the specified action may result in abandonment (e.g., filing a new complete appeal brief correcting deficiencies), a time period should be set for taking the specified action and, where appropriate, the action should specify that the provisions of 37 CFR 1.136 (or 1.136(a)) do not apply to that time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specified time limit should not be set simply to exclude the possibility of extending the period for reply under 37 CFR 1.136 unless that is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: specified time limit vs shortened statutory period (35 U.S.C. 133)
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified time for a particular action and a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133 are different: failure to meet a specified time results in loss of rights regarding that particular matter, whereas failure to reply within a shortened statutory period results in abandonment of the entire application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment of an application is not appealable, but a petition to revive may be granted if the delay was unavoidable (37 CFR 1.137(a)) or unintentional (37 CFR 1.137(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified time limits may be less than 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: As a specified time or time limit is not a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133, the Office may specify a time for taking action (or a time limit) of less than the 30 day minimum specified in 35 U.S.C. 133.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excusing short delays for specified time replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant replies a day or two after the specified time, the delay may be excused by the examiner if satisfactorily explained; the examiner may request an explanation if not apparent from the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast: a reply 1 day late in an application carrying a shortened statutory period under 35 U.S.C. 133 results in abandonment, no matter the excuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief time periods are not shortened statutory periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2-month period for filing an appeal brief (37 CFR 41.37(a)) and the 1-month period for filing a new appeal brief to correct deficiencies (37 CFR 41.37(d)) are time periods but are not shortened statutory periods under 35 U.S.C. 133; they are extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a) (up to 5 months) and, in exceptional situations, further under 1.136(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file an appeal brief (or new appeal brief) within the period set in 41.37(a) or (d) results in dismissal of the appeal; dismissal results in abandonment unless there are any allowed claim(s), in which case the examiner should cancel the nonallowed claims and allow the application. See MPEP § 1215.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to File Missing Parts reply period extendable
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2-month time period for reply to a Notice to File Missing Parts of an Application is not identified as a statutory period subject to 35 U.S.C. 133 and thus is extendable by up to 5 months under 37 CFR 1.136(a) and further under 1.136(b) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136(a) — extension by petition and fee (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period, applicant may extend the time period for reply up to the earlier of the expiration of any maximum period set by statute or five months after the time set for reply, if a petition for an extension of time and the fee set in § 1.17(a) are filed, unless exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include being notified otherwise in an Office action, replies that are appeal briefs under § 41.41, requests for oral hearing under § 41.47(a), replies to certain Board decisions (§ 1.304, § 41.50 or § 41.52), or when the application is involved in a contested case (§ 41.101(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of petition/fee controls extension period and amount
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which the petition and the fee have been filed is the date for purposes of determining the period of extension and the corresponding amount of the fee; the expiration of the time period is determined by the amount of the fee paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply must be filed prior to the expiration of the period of extension to avoid abandonment (§ 1.135). In no situation may applicant be granted an extension beyond the maximum time period set by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3) — constructive petitions and fee authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: A written request submitted in an application may be treated as incorporating a petition for extension of time for future replies; an authorization to charge required fees (including extension fees) will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension; submission of the fee set forth in § 1.17(a) will also be treated as a constructive petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This acts as a 'safety net' to avoid loss of rights for applicants who inadvertently omitted a petition but had previously filed an authorization or paid fees. The Office strongly recommends including a written petition with any desired extension to avoid processing delays. Example short petition language is provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136(b) — extensions for sufficient cause
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply cannot be filed within the time period and 1.136(a) is not available, the period for reply will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; requests must be filed on or before the day the reply is due and be accompanied by the petition fee under § 1.17(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extension can operate to extend the time beyond the maximum statutory period. Decisions on 1.136(b) requests are to be made by the Technology Center Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonextendable time periods after Notice of Allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is notified in a 'Notice of Allowability' that an application is otherwise in condition for allowance, the following time periods are not extendable if set in that Notice or in an Office action with a mail date on or after the Notice: (1) period for submitting an oath or declaration under § 1.63; (2) period for submitting formal drawings under § 1.85(c); (3) period for making a deposit under § 1.809(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are not available to correct such informalities; informalities must be corrected and issue/publication fees paid within the 3-month statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 1.136(a) extensions are not available
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time with the payment of a fee pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not available in: (A) reexamination proceedings (ex parte and inter partes exceptions noted), (B) all extensions during an interference proceeding (but not preparatory to an interference where a claim is suggested), (C) specific situations where an Office action states 1.136(a) is not applicable (e.g., reply to a notice of allowability, reissue apps associated with litigation, application in allowable condition with nonelected claims and time set to cancel such claims), and (D) limited instances where applicant is given a specified time limit to take certain actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See relevant MPEP sections and CFR citations for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension fees — cumulative, small entity reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees for extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(a) and are cumulative; a 50% reduction applies for small entities. If an applicant pays a 1-month fee and later needs an additional month, the proper fee is the amount for the two-month extension less the amount previously paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of replies filed after set period without petition/fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reply is filed after the set period and no petition or fee accompanies it, the reply will not be accepted as timely until the petition (which may be a constructive petition under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3)) and the appropriate fee are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If Office action sets a 3-month period, applicant replies in 4th month and includes only a 1-month extension petition, the reply is not acceptable until the fee is filed; if the fee is not filed until the 5th month an additional fee for the 2nd month is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies — no extension needed after timely first reply
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136 is not necessary when submitting a supplemental reply to an Office action if a complete first reply was timely filed in reply to the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of duplicate 1.136(b) requests and hand-carried limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for extension under 37 CFR 1.136(b) is filed in duplicate with a stamped return-addressed envelope, the Office will indicate action taken on the duplicate and return it promptly; hand-carried requests for extensions of time will no longer be accepted in the Technology Centers and must be delivered to the Customer Service Window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action taken should be noted on the original (filed) document and on the returned copy; notation on the original should be signed and identify the person granting or denying the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for late replies (7.98 / 7.98.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.98 (Reply Is Late, Extension of Time Suggested) and 7.98.01 (Reply Is Late, Extension of Time Suggested, Pro Se) may be used where a reply is filed late but an extension of time is possible; 7.98.01 includes language advising pro se applicants about petition and fee requirements and attaching the fee schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes indicate not to use 7.98 in reexamination or litigation-related reissue cases; enclose a photocopy of current fee schedule for pro se applicant actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions of time after payment of the issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory (nonextendable) time period for payment of the issue fee is 3 months from the date of the Notice of Allowance (35 U.S.C. 151); extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are NOT available to correct outstanding informalities when allowance is notified — informalities must be corrected and fee(s) paid within the 3-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two periods running — earlier statutory period not suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: When two different periods for reply are running against an application (one limited by the regular statutory period and the other by a limited period set in a subsequent Office action), the running of the first period is not suspended or affected by an ex parte limited time action or even by an appeal therefrom (except for the suggested claims exception in Chapter 2300).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying patent claims — controlling statutory period date
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims are copied from a patent and all of these claims are rejected, two different periods for reply may run; the controlling date of the statutory period is the date of the last unanswered Office action on the claims other than the copied patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Milton, 63 USPQ 132 (P.O. Super Exam. 1938) and MPEP Chapter 2300.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period ending on Saturday/Sunday/Federal holiday — next business day rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When the day or last day for taking any action or paying any fee falls on Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the action may be taken or the fee paid on the next succeeding secular or business day which is not a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday; this extends to the 12-month period for provisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP lists Federal holidays and explains that when a Federal holiday falls on a Sunday the following Monday is a holiday; when it falls on a Saturday the preceding Friday is considered a holiday for USPTO closure purposes. An amendment filed on the next business day should be endorsed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations when reply period is reset or restarted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a citation is incorrect or an Office action contains an error affecting applicant's ability to reply and this is called to the Office within 1 month of the mail date, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date the error is corrected (if requested by applicant). If called within the reply period but more than 1 month after the mail date, the Office will set a new period substantially equal to the time remaining; the new period must be at least 1 month. If error is called after expiration, the period will not be restarted and an extension fee will be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When remailing is necessary the action should be redated because the remailing date establishes the beginning of the period for reply. A supplementary action after a rejection explaining references or giving reasons more fully establishes a new date from which the statutory period runs. See MPEP §§505, 512, 513 and §707.05(g).
